evergreen.title: DON’T TAKE THE FIRST DRINK
evergreen.body: You never have to try to stop if you don’t start.

evergreen.title: KEEP TODAY SMALL
evergreen.body: Stay sober today. Tomorrow will get its own turn.

evergreen.title: CALL BEFORE THE CRISIS
evergreen.body: Reach out while the thought is still a thought.

evergreen.title: EAT SOMETHING
evergreen.body: Hunger can make an ordinary problem feel like the end of civilization.

evergreen.title: GET SOME REST
evergreen.body: Exhaustion is a terrible sponsor.

evergreen.title: CHANGE THE SCENE
evergreen.body: If the room is getting dangerous, leave the room.

evergreen.title: HAVE YOUR OWN RIDE
evergreen.body: Never let somebody else’s schedule decide when you can leave.

evergreen.title: KEEP AN EXIT PLAN
evergreen.body: Know where the door is before you need the door.

evergreen.title: BRING A SOBER PERSON
evergreen.body: Difficult events get easier when you don’t walk into them alone.

evergreen.title: KEEP SOMETHING IN YOUR HAND
evergreen.body: Coffee, soda, or water stops people from repeatedly offering you a drink.

evergreen.title: YOU DON’T OWE AN EXPLANATION
evergreen.body: “No thanks” is a complete answer.

evergreen.title: SKIP IT IF YOU NEED TO
evergreen.body: Protecting your sobriety is more important than protecting someone’s feelings.

evergreen.title: REMEMBER THE WHOLE STORY
evergreen.body: Don’t remember the first drink without remembering where it took you.

evergreen.title: DELAY THE DECISION
evergreen.body: You can reconsider anything tomorrow. Don’t drink today.

evergreen.title: BREAK THE HOUR DOWN
evergreen.body: When a day feels impossible, stay sober for the next ten minutes.

evergreen.title: USE THE PHONE
evergreen.body: That heavy little object becomes lighter after you dial somebody.

evergreen.title: GO WHERE RECOVERY IS
evergreen.body: When your thinking gets strange, put your body near sober people.

evergreen.title: KEEP YOUR ROUTINE
evergreen.body: Familiar sober actions can carry you through unfamiliar feelings.

evergreen.title: WATCH THE ISOLATION
evergreen.body: Canceling everything may feel like relief until your head becomes the entire meeting.

evergreen.title: FEELINGS AREN’T INSTRUCTIONS
evergreen.body: A feeling can be real without being a command.

evergreen.title: DON’T ARGUE WITH THE DRINK
evergreen.body: Thoughts come. Thoughts go. Acting on a thought is up to you.

evergreen.title: DO THE NEXT RIGHT THING
evergreen.body: Shower. Eat. Call. Walk. Pray. Get to a meeting. Whatever you have to.

evergreen.title: LOWER THE TEMPERATURE
evergreen.body: Not every disagreement needs to be settled tonight.

evergreen.title: AVOID MAJOR DECISIONS WHEN UPSET
evergreen.body: Stabilize first. Rearrange your life later.

evergreen.title: KEEP YOUR RECOVERY VISIBLE
evergreen.body: Save the numbers, meetings, readings, and people you may need quickly.

evergreen.title: BEWARE OF FEELING ‘CURED’
evergreen.body: Feeling good is a reason to continue—not a reason to stop.

evergreen.title: CELEBRATE WITHOUT TESTING YOURSELF
evergreen.body: Be careful: a good day does not make alcohol safer.

evergreen.title: ASK FOR HELP EARLY
evergreen.body: You do not need to earn help by falling apart first.

evergreen.title: START THE DAY ON PURPOSE
evergreen.body: Take one quiet moment before the world starts making demands.

evergreen.title: END THE DAY CLEAN
evergreen.body: Review it, release it, and put your head on the pillow sober.

evergreen.title: YOU’RE ALLOWED TO CHANGE YOUR MIND
evergreen.body: You are allowed to change your mind without defending yourself.

evergreen.title: WALK IN DRY PLACES
evergreen.body: Be careful—the hands can move faster than the mind.

evergreen.title: PEOPLE, PLACES & THINGS
evergreen.body: Emotional triggers are still triggers.

seasonal.title: A HOLIDAY IS COMING
seasonal.body: Decide where you’re going, who you’ll call, and how you’ll leave before the day arrives.

seasonal.title: HOLIDAY PLANS NEED AN EXIT PLAN
seasonal.body: Drive yourself, park where you can leave, and give yourself permission to go early.

seasonal.title: HOLIDAY STRESS COUNTS TOO
seasonal.body: Shopping, family, money, and expectations can pile up before the celebration even begins.

seasonal.title: YOU CAN DECLINE THE INVITATION
seasonal.body: Missing one gathering is better than losing your footing.

seasonal.title: FAMILY CAN PUSH OLD BUTTONS
seasonal.body: You are allowed to pause, step outside, call someone, or leave.

seasonal.title: THE DAY AFTER MATTERS
seasonal.body: Rest, eat, check in, and get around sober people after the excitement ends.

seasonal.title: NEW YEAR’S EVE IS JUST ONE NIGHT
seasonal.body: Make a sober plan, keep your own transportation, and leave before things get sloppy.

seasonal.title: START THE NEW YEAR SOBER
seasonal.body: You don’t need a dramatic reinvention. Wake up clear and do the next right thing.

seasonal.title: SUMMER EVENTS NEED SOBER PLANS
seasonal.body: Cookouts, concerts, and vacations still need an exit, a phone number, and something safe to drink.

seasonal.title: FOOTBALL SEASON CAN BE A DRINKING SEASON
seasonal.body: Watch the game somewhere your sobriety is normal—not something you have to defend.
